findings.evidence: In the DOM, the h2's parent is SPAN.duo-title. In the HTML standard, a span's content model is phrasing content and an h2 is not phrasing content. A summary may hold heading content directly ('phrasing content, optionally intermixed with heading content'), but not nested inside a span. Chrome's AX tree (ax.js) does expose 'heading level 2 REX + OLLIE', so heading navigation works in Chromium. The disclosure is announced as "TWO-PLAYER TESTS REX + OLLIE Ollie: Rex’s strength · 3.05 m · 3.01 t · Arm wrestle +" closed and '… –' open: the CSS glyph becomes part of the name, so a screen reader says 'plus' or 'dash' after the summary line.
findings.expected: Valid markup, so all browsers and assistive technologies expose the heading, and a disclosure name without the decorative glyph (the native expanded state already says open or closed).
findings.fix:
Replace the wrapper with heading content that a summary allows, for example

Two-player tests

(hgroup is heading content). Give the glyph empty alt text: content: "+" / ""; (and "–" / ""). The same alt-text fix applies to details.setup summary::after at line 97.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced. The h2#duo-title sits inside SPAN.duo-title inside SUMMARY. A span's content model is phrasing content and an h2 is not, so the markup is invalid; this is new in this change. Chromium still exposes 'heading level 2 REX + OLLIE', so no broken behaviour was shown there. The '+'/'–' glyph does end the disclosure's accessible name. That glyph pattern is not new: main's details.setup summaries are named 'Settings … –', 'Ollie … +' and 'Comic switches all off +'. The new summary repeats it. The reviewer's proposed hgroup fix makes things worse: in Chrome the hgroup (role group) drops out of the summary's name, so the disclosure becomes just 'Ollie: Rex’s strength · 3.05 m · 3.01 t · Arm wrestle', without 'Rex + Ollie'. Putting the eyebrow inside the h2 is valid and keeps the name.

findings.title: Their powers shows 'Growth form' and 'Grows over (s)' even when absorbed energy goes to the endless ocean: the page's own CSS overrides the hidden attribute (pre-existing, now inside the new panel; masked by shots.js)
findings.location: src/app.html:346 and 352 (#grow-fields is .field, #grow-t-row is .inline-num, both display:flex), set hidden at 798-799; test/shots.js:27 injects [hidden]{display:none!important}
findings.evidence: Script hidden.js, page wrapped with only the doctype and meta tags (as instructed), Their powers open at 1280 px: elements carrying the hidden attribute but still displayed are {"grow-fields":"flex h=238","grow-t-row":"flex h=42"}. Screenshot shots/aside-1280-light.png shows the growth-form chips, slider and 'Grows over (s) 60' under 'Endless ocean (canon)'. Main's build gives the same output (pre-existing). test/shots.js wraps the page with [hidden]{display:none!important}, so the suite never sees it.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced, and it predates this change: main shows it identically, and main's shots.js already had the masking rule. #grow-fields (.field) and #grow-t-row (.inline-num) are display:flex in the page's CSS, which overrides the browser's [hidden]{display:none}. Setting .hidden at src/app.html:798-799 therefore does nothing, and with 'Endless ocean (canon)' selected, Their powers shows the Growth form chips, the slider and 'Grows over (s) 60'. The hidden #grow-t and #grow-s inputs also take keyboard focus: a Shift+Tab trace from Rex's tabs landed on grow-t, then grow-s. The repo's sibling test (build-comparison/test/shots.js:27) states that the artifact host's skeleton has no [hidden] rule and the page must hide its own hidden elements; build-comparison fixed the same defect that way after its round-1 review. So the live page shows this, and Rex's test/shots.js:27 masks it by injecting [hidden]{display:none!important}. It counts here because this change moves these controls into the new Their powers panel.
verdict.better_fix: Add [hidden] { display: none !important; } near the top of the stylesheet in src/app.html. Remove [hidden]{display:none!important} from the skeleton in test/shots.js:27, matching build-comparison/test/shots.js, so the test sees the page as the host serves it. Optionally add a shots.js check that no element with the hidden attribute has a non-zero box.

findings.outcome: Fixed: [hidden] { display: none !important; } in the page's own stylesheet; shots.js no longer adds it and fails on any hidden element that takes space.
